newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Lehman sells private Swiss bank to Canadian group.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sells private Swiss bank to Canadian group.

text.p: U.S. brokerage house Lehman Brothers has sold its fully-owned private Swiss bank in Geneva to a Canadian group for an undisclosed sum, a senior bank official said on Thursday.

Urs Brander, director general of Lehman Brothers Bank Switzerland based in Geneva, told Reuters Canadian asset management and financial services group MFC Financial Corp, based in Vancouver, bought the bank.
Brander said he would stay as head of the bank, which has a staff of 15. The bank will be renamed MFC Merchant Bank SA.
"We will continue our business in private banking and asset management," he said
"This is a strategic reorientation of Lehman Brothers. They are concentrating more on their brokerage and new issues business and to a lesser degree, on private banking," he said.
Brander gave no details. He said the bank did not publish its results in Switzerland, but banking sources said 1996 was not a profitable year for the bank.
